approved: Introduced the sixth Statute Stocktake Bill since 1998, repealing 84 redundant annual Appropriation Acts spanning 1 July 1999 to 30 June 2010, following on from a 2012 act that had already repealed 93 earlier Appropriation Acts and 35 Supply Acts.

Argued that the Statute Stocktake (Appropriations) Bill 2013 would repeal 84 redundant annual appropriation acts and related laws without easing the regulatory burden on business, criticised the government's record on regulation, and supported a coalition agenda to remove regulation costing the community $1 billion annually.

Supported the Statute Stocktake (Appropriations) Bill 2013, which would repeal 84 old annual appropriation acts from 1999-2000 to 2009-10 inclusive, and noted that the coalition supports 87.3 per cent of bills before the House.

Explained the Statute Stocktake (Appropriations) Bill 2013, the sixth such bill since 1998, will repeal 84 old annual appropriation acts dating from 1999 to 2010 without affecting agency funding, and rejected opposition claims of red tape, noting the Howard government's GST created the biggest regulatory burden on small business.

The coalition supported the Statute Stocktake (Appropriations) Bill 2013, a housekeeping bill repealing 84 redundant appropriation acts from July 1999 to June 2010. It criticised the government's deregulation claims, citing that the Rudd-Gillard Labor governments added about 21,000 new regulations and repealed only 104 since 2008.
